commands.author: Pick-cat

target.title: fix(codex): align computer wait duration parse with computer-tool
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex computer `wait` / `hold_key` outer watchdog deadlines used JavaScript `Number(...)` on free-form `duration` values. Hex strings such as `"0x10"` were accepted (`Number(\"0x10\") === 16`) and silently inflated the deadline, while the downstream computer tool already rejects hex via `readFiniteNumberParam` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber`.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Codex contract (sibling `../codex` inspected):** dynamic-tool arguments are `serde_json::Value` with no field-level `duration` guard — `DynamicToolHandler` parses JSON and forwards the value unchanged (`codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs:136`, checkout `bdd282f3bbd55df3a869a5438519cd948c134d4d`). OpenClaw pins `@openai/codex@0.144.4`.

**Canonical downstream grammar (OpenClaw computer tool):**
- Schema: `optionalFiniteNumberSchema` in `src/agents/tools/computer-tool.ts:161`
- Runtime: `readFiniteNumberParam` → `readNumberParam({ strict: true })` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber` (`src/agents/tools/common.ts:228`, `computer-tool.ts:856`)

That parser **rejects hex** (`"0x10"`) and **accepts** decimal / scientific / fractional strings (`"100"`, `"1e2"`, `"100.5"`, `"0.5"`) plus finite numbers.

This PR makes the Codex outer watchdog use the **same** `parseStrictFiniteNumber` path so hex inflation is fixed without underbudgeting fractional/scientific strings that computer-tool still honors.

Collision: overlaps [#107623](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107623); this head is the rebased, contract-aligned form.

## User Impact

| Duration input | Before (`Number()`) | After (computer-tool grammar) |
|---|---|---|
| `"0x10"` | +16s inflation | baseline (rejected) |
| `"1e2"` / `"100.5"` / `"0.5"` | coerced | honored (aligned) |
| `0.5` (number) | honored | honored |

## Evidence

Exact head: `d85b72dabe57770b68e901f974a448729cf05581`

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ keeps explicit dynamic tool timeouts above the default bridge deadline
 ✓ ignores partial dynamic tool timeout strings
 ✓ honors timeoutSeconds when timeoutMs is absent
 ✓ prefers timeoutMs over timeoutSeconds
 ✓ ignores non-positive timeoutSeconds
 ✓ rejects fractional timeoutSeconds and falls back to the default
 ✓ uses configured image generation timeouts for Codex dynamic tool calls
 ✓ uses default media and message dynamic tool deadlines
 ✓ aligns computer duration strings with computer-tool parseStrictFiniteNumber
 ✓ uses media image config and caps excessive dynamic tool timeouts
 ✓ uses a 90 second default for generic Codex dynamic tool calls
 ✓ returns a failed dynamic tool response when an app-server tool call exceeds the deadline
 ✓ marks a timeout during pre-execution hooks as unstarted
 ✓ delegates an unpublished abort boundary to the terminal observer
 ✓ uses a conservative dispatched fallback without a terminal observer
 ✓ lets a structured sessions_send timeout win after setup work
 ✓ reports pre-execution cancellations to the private result observer
 ✓ preserves enclosing timeout provenance for pre-execution aborts
 ✓ classifies app-server client closure as a failed tool outcome
 ✓ preserves enclosing timeout provenance for active tool aborts
 ✓ preserves timeout provenance when the dynamic tool bridge rejects
 ✓ contains hostile rejected values while notifying the private observer
 ✓ contains hostile abort reasons while notifying the private observer
 ✓ logs process poll timeout context separately from session idle
 ✓ does not split surrogate pairs when truncating timeout log fields
 ✓ keeps async-start metadata on internal dynamic tool progress only
 ✓ allows turn release after successful terminal dynamic tool responses
 ✓ resolves terminal dynamic tool batch state
 ✓ does not let async-start tool results block terminal side-effect batches

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  30 passed (30)
```

Parser contract sample (`parseStrictFiniteNumber` vs `Number`):

```
{"v":"0x10","Number":16}                    # strict → undefined / baseline
{"v":"1e2","Number":100,"parseStrictFiniteNumber":100}
{"v":"100.5","Number":100.5,"parseStrictFiniteNumber":100.5}
{"v":"0.5","Number":0.5,"parseStrictFiniteNumber":0.5}
```

Codex files checked: `../codex/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs:127-142`.
